sentences.zh: Why?

sentences.zh: 因为纳粹的流程要运作，即人员的处理量要达标，就必须以平稳、有序的方式进行。

sentences.en: Those Jews must get off those trains, they must allow themselves to be organised into columns, they must go through the process of selection to the left.

sentences.en: If you are old or too young or in any way weak, or you are a mother with children, you go to the left, where you will be taken to the gas chambers.
sentences.zh: 如果你年事已高、太过年幼、身体虚弱，或者你是带着孩子的母亲，就往左走，你们会被带去毒气室。

sentences.en: These people have no weapons, their children, their kids, of course not.

sentences.zh: 考虑到纳粹设计的方法，这对他们来说将是极其困难的。

sentences.en: It would, as you say, snarl it up.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这会把事情搞砸。

sentences.en: And so in this quite chilling image, Rudi would use when later talking about this, he would say, it is much easier to kill sheep than to hunt pigs or deer.
sentences.zh: 因此，在鲁迪后来谈及此事时，他用了一个相当令人不寒而栗的比喻，他说，杀羊比猎猪或猎鹿要容易得多。

sentences.en: And what he meant by that, as a boy who'd grown up in the Slovak countryside, was that a column of sheep marching into the abattoir can be handled, you can manage big numbers.
sentences.zh: 作为一个在斯洛伐克乡村长大的男孩，他的意思是，一群羊走进屠宰场是可以控制的，你可以处理大量的数量。

sentences.en: But if you are a hunter picking off individual deer on the hillside, that takes time and you will miss a lot.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个在山坡上猎杀个别鹿的猎人，那需要时间，而且你会错过很多。

sentences.en: And so what he envisaged was that if Jews arrived knowing they were being led to their death, they would then panic.
sentences.zh: 所以他设想的是，如果犹太人在抵达时就知道自己被带去送死，他们就会恐慌。

sentences.en: Some would run off in this way, some would run off in that way.
sentences.zh: 有些人会往这边跑，有些人会往那边跑。

sentences.en: Yes, most of them would be gunned down, but it would be chaos.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们中的大多数人会被枪杀，但这会造成混乱。

sentences.en: And in that chaos, some might survive.
sentences.zh: 而在那种混乱中，有些人可能会幸存下来。

sentences.en: And so that's why the Nazis, even at the moment when the doors are locking of the gas chamber, they are being told by their captors, get yourself

sentences.en: clean now, enjoy bathing, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 洗干净，享受沐浴等等。

sentences.en: They do not, even at the last moment, want the panic that could slow down, that could throw sand in the gears of the machine.

sentences.en: And that is what leads Rudolf over to make the crucial decision, which is, if deception is the central element of this killing

sentences.en: machine, then the only way to throw some sand in the gears of the machine is to tear through that veil of ignorance that the Jews of Europe have.
sentences.zh: 机器的核心要素，那么给机器齿轮撒沙子的唯一方法，就是撕开欧洲犹太人所处的无知面纱。

sentences.en: That means somebody has to get out and tell them what

sentences.en: And he decides with that wonderful arrogance of youth, that person might as well be me.
sentences.zh: 他带着年轻人那种奇妙的傲慢，认定那个人选非我莫属。

sentences.en: Just before we get to the escape, he's in a position to observe the workings of the machine because he's in Canada.
sentences.zh: 就在我们谈到逃亡之前，他因为身处加拿大区，得以观察到这台机器的运作方式。

sentences.en: He's an assistant registrar, and then he's the camp clerk, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他先是助理登记员，后来又成了营地文书，对吧？

sentences.en: So Tom and I were actually talking about this earlier, weren't we, between ourselves.
sentences.zh: 汤姆和我之前其实私下里讨论过这个问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: So this is such a difficult question, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棘手的问题，对吧？

sentences.zh: 那些身处加拿大区的人，我是说，如果你……用这个词不太准确。

sentences.en: So, you know, well, it is just the wrong word, but they are, they are collaborating with the machine.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，好吧，这确实用词不当，但他们确实是在与这台机器合作。

sentences.zh: 他们在协助它运作，不是吗？

sentences.en: This is a, this is an impossible situation to be in.
sentences.zh: 这是一种……这是一种无法摆脱的绝境。

sentences.en: Or are most of them still ignorant?

sentences.zh: 鲁迪本人确实对此深思熟虑。

sentences.zh: 我是说，晚年时，鲁迪会对其他奥斯威辛的幸存者非常怀疑，如果他之前不认识他们的话，因为他会想：他们为了活下来都做了些什么？

sentences.en: You know, jumping ahead, Fred Wetzler, who is his partner in escape, married a survivor of Auschwitz and relations between Fred and Rudi became very strained in
sentences.zh: 你知道，跳过这一段，弗雷德·韦茨勒，也就是他逃亡时的同伴，娶了一位奥斯威辛的幸存者，弗雷德和鲁迪之间的关系变得非常紧张，

sentences.en: part because Rudi was very suspicious of Fred's wife because she was an Auschwitz survivor.
sentences.zh: 部分原因就是鲁迪对弗雷德的妻子非常怀疑，因为她也是奥斯威辛的幸存者。

sentences.en: A very difficult thought to grapple with, but he thought, what did you do to survive?
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难面对的想法，但他会想：你为了生存做了什么？

sentences.zh: 通常是普通罪犯，身上标着绿色三角形，而不是黄色星星。

sentences.zh: 在奥斯威辛，你记得有一整套颜色编码的三角形系统，粉色三角形是著名的同性恋囚犯，黄色星星显然是犹太人，红色是政治犯。

sentences.en: Green triangle would put the fear of God into a prisoner like Rudi because that was a common criminal, often murderers, who were the most brutal henchmen.
sentences.zh: 绿色三角形会让像鲁迪这样的囚犯感到恐惧，因为那是普通罪犯，通常是杀人犯，他们是最残暴的打手。

sentences.en: They were the, you know, the SS would police the camp with weapons.
sentences.zh: 他们是……你知道，党卫军会用武器来监管营地。

sentences.zh: 卡波，尤其是绿色三角形那一群人，会带着棍棒，他们甚至会进行体育比赛，看能不能一拳打死一个囚犯？

sentences.en: You know, Rudi witnessed that to, you know, a single punch to knock out and kill a

sentences.zh: 说你意识到所有这些关于奥斯威辛的事情是你以前不知道的。

sentences.en: I mean, it was news to me that there was a really organised Auschwitz resistance and underground.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对我来说，奥斯威辛有一个真正组织严密的抵抗运动和地下组织，这还是新闻。

sentences.en: They got secured jobs for their people in those places.
sentences.zh: 他们为自己人在那些地方争取到了职位。

sentences.zh: 他们确实不仅提高了生活质量，还提高了在奥斯威辛的预期寿命。

sentences.en: The concentration camp did rise.

sentences.en: Meanwhile, adjoining the Auschwitz concentration camp is the death camp, the gas chambers, the crematoria, and that is continuing at a huge pace.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，毗邻奥斯威辛集中营的是死亡营、毒气室、火葬场，而那里的屠杀正以惊人的速度持续进行。

sentences.en: And what Rudi realizes, again, with that great clarity that he seems to have as a very young man is, well, in a very perverse way, the smooth functioning of this
sentences.zh: 鲁迪意识到，再次以他作为一个年轻人似乎拥有的那种极大的清晰度意识到，好吧，以一种非常扭曲的方式，这个

sentences.en: concentration camp, where the death rate is now falling, is actually having a knock-on effect
sentences.zh: 死亡率正在下降的集中营的平稳运作，实际上对

sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，他意识到抵抗运动，如果说有什么影响的话，那就是让更多的犹太人在死亡营部分被杀害。

sentences.zh: 于是他开始想，听着，

sentences.en: He has seen how it's ignorance on the part of the deportees of their fate that enables them to be processed.

sentences.en: You have this incredibly moving detail about how they find an old chemistry book, him and a friend, and they kind of study it as though it's the most precious thing in the world.

sentences.en: And the Jewish leadership in Slovakia made the, you know, not all of them, some wouldn't go along with it, but they made a decision to do it.
sentences.zh: 斯洛伐克的犹太领导层做出了决定，你知道，并非所有人，有些人不愿配合，但他们最终决定照做。

sentences.en: And Walter, you know, Rudy, hugely resented them, actually, because the order, for example, to turn up that initial deportation order, it came, as it were,
sentences.zh: 而沃尔特，也就是鲁迪，实际上非常怨恨他们，因为例如那份最初的驱逐令，它就像是

sentences.en: on Jewish community headed notepaper, and he wrote on their letterhead, you know, and he remembered
sentences.zh: 印在犹太社区的信笺上，他写在他们的信头上，你知道，他记得

sentences.en: that and thought, well, you know, how can I possibly trust these people with the information I have, and yet didn't really know who else to bring it to?
sentences.zh: 这一点，心想，我怎么可能把掌握的信息托付给这些人呢？但又不知道还能带给谁？

sentences.en: What he didn't know was that in the, within the official Jewish leadership, a large group of that same body of people were also engaged
sentences.zh: 他所不知道的是，在官方犹太领导层内部，那群人中的很大一部分人也参与了

sentences.en: and resistance activities, and they called themselves the working group.
sentences.zh: 抵抗活动，他们自称为“工作组”。

sentences.en: And they were also engaged in illicit underground activities.
sentences.zh: 他们也从事非法的地下活动。

sentences.en: So these were the sorts of hideous moral dilemmas that people were thrown into, where, you know, you can see with your own eyes that your fellow Jews
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是人们陷入的那种可怕的道德困境，你可以亲眼看到你的犹太同胞

sentences.en: aren't going to be bundled on trains and deported.
sentences.zh: 即将被塞进火车并被驱逐。

sentences.en: Do you allow that to happen brutally, or do you allow it to happen where you have some hand in it, and perhaps can dilute the edict some way?
sentences.zh: 你是任由这种残酷的事情发生，还是参与其中，或许能以某种方式减轻法令的影响？

sentences.en: None of us can know what we would decide.
sentences.zh: 我们谁都不知道自己会做出什么决定。

sentences.en: None of us can judge, I don't think, what was right or wrong in that situation.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们谁都无法评判在那样的处境下什么是对，什么是错。

sentences.en: Rudy himself was very judgmental and judged those people very harshly for what they did.
sentences.zh: 鲁迪本人非常爱评判，对那些人的所作所为评价非常严苛。

sentences.en: But he does make contact through an amazing series of scrapes, really, you know, one point
sentences.zh: 但他确实通过一系列惊人的磨难取得了联系，真的，你知道，有一次

sentences.en: involving he and Fred dressing up as Slovak sort of pig herds and helping transport a farmer, a good man who helps them.
sentences.zh: 他和弗雷德打扮成斯洛伐克的养猪人，帮助运送一位好心的农民，那个人帮助了他们。

sentences.en: They dress up as his pig herds and bundle a whole lot of pigs onto a train and thereby go to a local regional meat market, livestock market, and there make contact with
sentences.zh: 他们装扮成他的养猪人，把一大群猪赶上火车，借此前往当地的肉类市场、牲畜市场，并在那里与

sentences.en: a Jewish doctor who leads them to the Jewish, underground Jewish leadership.
sentences.zh: 一位犹太医生取得了联系，医生将他们引向了犹太地下领导层。

sentences.en: And from there, they are transferred to a small town of Zilina, where, and I've stood in this room,
sentences.zh: 从那里，他们被转移到日利纳的一个小镇，在那里——我曾站在那个房间里——

sentences.en: in the basement of the Jewish old people's home in Zilina, for the best part of a fortnight, they are in secret, in hiding, debriefed.
sentences.zh: 在日利纳犹太老人院的地下室里，他们秘密躲藏了整整两周，接受了详细询问。

sentences.en: And there has to be in hiding.
sentences.zh: 而且必须躲藏起来。

sentences.en: These are now wanted men.
sentences.zh: 他们现在是通缉犯。

sentences.en: And I reproduce in the book, the SS Gestapo telegram.
sentences.zh: 我在书中重现了那份党卫军盖世太保的电报。

sentences.en: The telegram goes from the SS to the
sentences.zh: 电报从党卫军发给

sentences.en: Gestapo saying, you know, these men are on the run and are wanted.
sentences.zh: 盖世太保，说这些人正在逃亡，是通缉犯。

sentences.en: And this would have been put up on the bulletin board of every Gestapo office across the Nazi empire, across Europe, you know,
sentences.zh: 这会被张贴在纳粹帝国各地、整个欧洲的每一个盖世太保办公室的公告栏上，你知道，

sentences.en: Walter Israel Rosenberg and Alfred Israel Wetzler.
sentences.zh: 沃尔特·以色列·罗森伯格和阿尔弗雷德·以色列·韦茨勒。
zh_words: 沃尔特·以色列·罗森伯格
阿尔弗雷德·以色列·韦茨勒

sentences.en: The Nazis insisted that every Jewish man, if his first name was not identifiably Jewish, adopt the name Israel as a middle name.
sentences.zh: 纳粹坚持要求每一位犹太男性，如果其名字不是明显的犹太名字，就必须采用“以色列”作为中间名。

sentences.en: And so you see that in this telegram.
sentences.zh: 所以你在那份电报中看到了这一点。

sentences.en: But they're in hiding.
sentences.zh: 但他们当时在躲藏。

sentences.en: The information they have gathered pours out of them.
sentences.zh: 他们收集的信息从他们口中倾泻而出。

sentences.en: They cannot stop.
sentences.zh: 他们无法停止。

sentences.en: I mean, Rudy has memorised up to five transports a day for the best part of two
sentences.zh: 我是说，鲁迪记住了长达两年时间里，每天多达五次的运输情况，

sentences.en: years, the estimated number, the point of origin, and even the sort of serial number allocated to the
sentences.zh: 估计的人数、出发点，甚至分配给

sentences.en: handful of prisoners on each transport who were selected to live and become slave labourers.
sentences.zh: 每一批运输中被选中活下来成为奴隶劳工的那少数囚犯的序列号。

sentences.en: Those numbers that are famously tattooed on the arm.
sentences.zh: 那些著名的纹在手臂上的数字。

sentences.en: So he can say 8, 7, 500 up to 8, 7, 700 is a transport from, say, you know, Grodno in Poland in August of 1943 or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以他能说出87500到87700号是来自，比如，1943年8月波兰格罗德诺的运输，诸如此类。

sentences.en: He's memorised them all.
sentences.zh: 他把这些全都记住了。

sentences.en: And so every word that comes out of them is taken down as if in dictation by a man who works for the, you know, Jewish leadership.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说的每一个字，都被一个为犹太领导层工作的人像听写一样记录下来。

sentences.en: And he writes a very dry, strictly factual, 32-page, single-spaced account of what's happened.
sentences.zh: 他写了一份非常枯燥、严格基于事实、32页、单倍行距的事件记录。

sentences.en: Reading your account of it, you say that it describes so much that we associate, you know, that Auschwitz conjures up.
sentences.zh: 读到你的记录时，你说它描述了太多我们与奥斯威辛联系在一起的东西。

sentences.en: The life of an Auschwitz prisoner, the topography of the camps, initial journey by cattle truck, the shaving of heads and bodies, the tattooing of numbers,
sentences.zh: 奥斯威辛囚犯的生活、营地的地形、最初的运牛车之旅、剃光头和体毛、纹身编号、

sentences.en: the colour-coded triangles, the barracks, the inner and outer chain of watchtowers, the roll call,
sentences.zh: 颜色编码的三角形、营房、内外两层岗哨、点名、

sentences.en: the sign saying Arbeit might fry, the slave factories, the hanging of attempted escapees, the starvation, the casual beatings, all of it.
sentences.zh: 写着“劳动带来自由”的标语、奴隶工厂、绞死试图逃跑的人、饥饿、随意的殴打，所有这些。

sentences.en: So all of that is in there.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些都在里面。

sentences.en: But I was startled when you say that the word gas didn't appear until page 7.
sentences.zh: 但我很惊讶你说“毒气”这个词直到第7页才出现。

sentences.en: And its core revelation that all but a small number of Jewish deportees for Auschwitz were murdered on arrival didn't come until page 8.
sentences.zh: 而其核心揭露——即绝大多数被驱逐到奥斯威辛的犹太人在抵达时就被杀害了——直到第8页才出现。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that's, it's, again, it's this kind of weird combination of the, I mean, the unbelievable horror of what is being described.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，这又是一种奇怪的结合，即所描述的令人难以置信的恐怖，

sentences.en: And yet, evidently, this kind of almost bureaucratic, punctilious attention to detail.
sentences.zh: 然而显然，又有一种近乎官僚主义的、一丝不苟的细节关注。

sentences.en: I think that's probably on Oskar Krasniansky, who compiles the report.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概要归功于负责整理报告的奥斯卡·克拉斯尼扬斯基。
zh_words: 奥斯卡·克拉斯尼扬斯基

sentences.en: He's no writer, and he's no journalist, and he doesn't order the verbatim words that have come out of these two young men in the way that I think any of us would.
sentences.zh: 他不是作家，也不是记者，他没有按照我认为我们任何一个人会采用的方式来整理这两个年轻人说出的原话。

sentences.en: Instead, oddly, he decides to sort of frame it chronologically.
sentences.zh: 相反，奇怪的是，他决定按时间顺序来构建它。

sentences.en: So each one, Wetzler and then Werber, describe chronologically what happened to them, starting
sentences.zh: 所以韦茨勒和韦尔伯每个人都按时间顺序描述了他们身上发生的事情，从

sentences.en: with their, you know, arrival in the transit camps, Novakii in Slovakia, in Rudi's case, and Serep in
sentences.zh: 他们抵达中转营开始，鲁迪的情况是斯洛伐克的诺瓦基，韦茨勒的情况是

sentences.en: Wetzler's case.
sentences.zh: 塞雷德。

sentences.en: And then that's why partly it takes you till page 7 before you actually get the kind of the lead, you know.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你读到第7页才真正看到那种核心内容的原因。

sentences.en: And it's very, it's frustrating to read in that sense, because you just want to, you think it should grab the reader by the scruff of the neck.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，读起来很令人沮丧，因为你只是想，你认为它应该抓住读者的衣领（引起震撼）。

sentences.en: I think what was going on there was a sense and awareness that this will be unbelievable to people reading it.
sentences.zh: 我认为当时的情况是一种意识，即人们读到这些会感到难以置信。

sentences.en: And therefore, if you start with the sort of headline, as it were, it would be too easily dismissed.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你从所谓的头条新闻开始，它太容易被驳回了。

sentences.en: And therefore, it needed to be assembled sort of methodically, where, you know, it's first one fact, then the next fact, then the next until they build.
sentences.zh: 因此，它需要有条不紊地组装起来，你知道，先是一个事实，然后是下一个，再下一个，直到它们建立起来。

sentences.en: And, you know, between them, Oskar Krasniansky, who compiles the report, he's actually an engineer, and he's his boss in the Jewish council, Oskar Neumann, is a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 而且，整理报告的奥斯卡·克拉斯尼扬斯基实际上是一名工程师，他在犹太委员会的上司奥斯卡·诺伊曼是一名律师。
zh_words: 奥斯卡·克拉斯尼扬斯基

sentences.en: And so between them, an engineer and a lawyer, neither of these are people interested in telling a sort of gripping story.
sentences.zh: 所以他们两个，一个工程师和一个律师，都不是那种有兴趣讲述引人入胜故事的人。

sentences.en: They are rather interested in presenting a, you know, chronological sequence of fact, and a kind of anatomy of this factory of death, which is something nobody has
sentences.zh: 他们更感兴趣的是呈现一个事实的时间顺序，以及这种死亡工厂的解剖结构，这是人类历史上从未有人

sentences.en: ever known in human history before.
sentences.zh: 知道过的东西。

sentences.en: And so this document is drawn up.
sentences.zh: 于是这份文件就这样起草了。

sentences.en: And who does it go to?
sentences.zh: 它被送到了谁的手里？

sentences.en: And what is their reaction?
sentences.zh: 他们的反应是什么？

sentences.en: So the report is finally finished.
sentences.zh: 报告终于完成了。

sentences.en: And it embarks on a journey of its own, almost in a kind of escape journey of its own.
sentences.zh: 它开始了属于它自己的旅程，几乎就像是一场逃亡之旅。

sentences.en: And I think my book is the first time in one place that's ever been assembled, the actual route it took.
sentences.zh: 我认为我的书是第一次将它所走的实际路线汇集在一个地方。

sentences.en: It is a gripping yarn, I think, in its own right, because it then has to be smuggled hand to hand across borders, across occupied Europe.
sentences.zh: 我认为它本身就是一个引人入胜的故事，因为它必须被手递手地走私过边境，穿过被占领的欧洲。

sentences.en: You know, anybody who's found holding this thing would immediately themselves be, you know, imprisoned or worse by the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 你知道，任何被发现持有这东西的人，自己都会立即被纳粹监禁或更糟。

sentences.en: And so it's a very dangerous document.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一份非常危险的文件。

sentences.en: And how it gets smuggled across Europe is, to me, riveting, where, you know, I have the account of a woman who, you know, is literally in
sentences.zh: 它是如何被走私过欧洲的，对我来说非常引人入胜，你知道，我有一位女士的叙述，她真的在

sentences.zh: 阁楼的一个小房间里，秘密地把它翻译成匈牙利语。

sentences.en: You know, there are figures in the resistance who meet each other at an art gallery and smuggle.
sentences.zh: 你知道，抵抗组织里有人在美术馆见面并进行走私。

sentences.en: One copy is surreptitiously moved from the briefcase of one resistance man into the briefcase of the other, so that no one will see the handoff of the documents.
sentences.zh: 一份副本被秘密地从一个抵抗组织成员的公文包转移到另一个人的公文包里，这样就不会有人看到文件的交接。

sentences.en: You know, this is a red-hot piece, a document that has to be handled with great care,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一份极其敏感的文件，必须非常小心地处理，

sentences.en: improbably, incredibly, through a whole, you know, procession of sometimes ridiculous characters.
sentences.zh: 不可思议地，通过一连串有时甚至有些荒唐的人物。

sentences.zh: 你知道，我们有温斯顿·丘吉尔在送达他手中的文件摘要上的潦草批注，他写道：能做什么，能说什么，仿佛被他所看到的惊得几乎
